reason: Internal: design bundle only, no code. Records the operator decision on Step 1 of design/evaluation/ — option 1, name the slot: a new layer above nora.app inside the nora root package so the contracts can see it. Probed before recording rather than after. The layer holds: lint-imports reports six contracts kept with the new package importing nora.app.composition and nora.config, and the reverse direction, nora.app importing the new package, is correctly refused as one broken contract, which is the property that matters. The probe is also why the edit list has three items instead of one. Two of them are visible only by probing: the only app and __main__ read config contract lists its source modules explicitly, so a new package is unconstrained by default and the probe read config with nothing objecting; and EVALS_ALLOWED_NORA_PACKAGES in tests/test_boundaries.py must gain the new name. The probe additionally established which of the two evals gates actually binds — with evals importing the new package, the import-linter contract named evals may only reach nora.app and nora.testing reported KEPT while only the boundary test caught it. That is not a defect but documented behaviour at pyproject.toml line 268, where allow_indirect_imports is load-bearing because nora.app legitimately imports half the tree; the same comment names the boundary test as the allowlist backstop. So a green lint-imports is not proof the evals boundary held, which is the shape this bundle is about appearing inside its own first step. The working name nora.harness is open and collides with two things it replaces.
